caption: Figure X: figure showing the hazard ratio of death per standard deviation of the ECG and EHR scores in days 0 to 30 and days 31 to 365 after discharge, from the registered primary analysis (2,909 discharges, EHR+ECG cohort), with 95% patient-level bootstrap intervals from 2,000 refits. The ECG's early to late ratio is 1.26 (1.06 to 1.51).

Figure X: figure showing the ratio of the ECG score's hazard ratio for death in days 0 to 30 after discharge to that in days 31 to 365, in the registered primary analysis and each sensitivity analysis, with 95% patient-level bootstrap intervals. Values above 1 mean the ECG's signal is concentrated early. The three-modality analyses use 1,405 discharges. The others use the EHR+ECG cohort.

Figure X: figure showing the calibration of the at-diagnosis model for death at 30 and 365 days after admission (EHR+ECG cohort, 3,501 admissions). Lines are loess calibration curves with 95% patient-clustered bootstrap bands; points are deciles of predicted risk, merged from the lowest until each holds at least 10 events. The dashed line marks perfect calibration. Calibration slope 1.02 at 30 days and 1.02 at 365 days; integrated calibration index 0.008 and 0.018.
